[mathematical] Normalization of the conditional Gaussian uses an undefined or ambiguous dimension \(N\)

**Where:** Supplementary Material, Sec. B, Eq. (B.7).
**What is wrong:** The denominator is written as \((2\pi)^{N/2}\sqrt{\det(M^{-1})}\). Earlier, the paper defines \(\mu\) to run from \(1\) to \(2N_{\rm mode}\), so the dimension of \(B\) is \(D=2N_{\rm mode}\). If \(N\) in Eq. **Concrete fix:** Define \(D\equiv 2N_{\rm mode}\) and write
\[
P(B|\theta,d,\emptyset)=
\frac{\exp[-\frac12(B-\hat B)^\mu M_{\mu\nu}(B-\hat B)^\nu]}
{(2\pi)^{D/2}\sqrt{\det(M^{-1})}} .
\]
